Hello! We are  Plutopia, and our mission is to turn raw space data in to real-world product that helps society as a whole!

We have experience with SAR data handling , GEE and ML training as well as hardware experience
summary:
TerraKey is a mobile web app, in English and Vietnamese, that turns NASA Earth data into a crop-rotation plan for one specific field. Smallholder farmers in river deltas and lowlands face worsening salt intrusion, drought and months of bare soil. Yet many still plant the same crop on the same calendar, because generic advice does not fit their land. We start with Vietnam’s Mekong Delta as our pilot region and are building the system so it can expand to other farming regions.

A farmer pins their field on a satellite map and answers a few questions about crops, water, goals and limits. TerraKey then compares three plans: keep as now, fill the bare months, or swap the weakest crop. Every suggestion is checked against that field’s own NASA rain, temperature, soil moisture and plant-growth history. The engine never places a crop in a high-risk month. The chosen plan becomes a month-by-month calendar. When NASA data or our machine-learning forecast shows a risk, a backup plan appears with the likelihood, a confidence score and one change the farmer can accept or undo. An optional field sensor adds plot-level soil zones (for microzones), but the app works fully on NASA data alone.
details:
What it does. TerraKey helps Mekong Delta smallholders decide what to plant, and when, on their own field. Setup takes about four minutes:

  • pin or draw the field on a satellite map
  • list the crops and months, pre-filled from MODIS greenness
  • pick the top two goals: save water, build soil, break pests or income
  • add water source and problem months, drainage, and limits such as labour or no buyer for a new crop

The app then shows:

  • Three plans side by side, comparing soil organic matter, yield, profit, water use, bare months and stress months.
  • Evidence for every crop: each one checked against the field’s own rain, temperature, salt and drainage, with numbered sources.
  • A Rotation Domino showing how one crop choice affects the next seasons.
  • A month-by-month calendar for the chosen plan.
  • A backup plan that appears when a risk is detected.
  • A Soil Health Report with a NASA-only score, plot micro-zones and 12-month NASA trends.

How it works. A Python pipeline downloads and cleans NASA data for 36 grid cells covering the delta:

  • POWER weather from 1981
  • GPM IMERG rainfall
  • SMAP root-zone soil moisture
  • MODIS NDVI and evapotranspiration
  • GRACE groundwater
  • SRTM elevation

It then computes FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration, weekly normals and drought triggers.

A 30-day forecast (XGBoost and a GRU network) was trained on 2001–2018 and tested on 2022–2025, years it never saw. It cut errors by 55% for soil wetness and 51% for hot days, compared with the 25-year average for that time of year.

The crop engine tests 21 crops at every possible start month in each bare gap. It checks growing season length, water need and salt tolerance (FAO), temperature, drainage, labour and pest breaks. It only suggests crops that face zero stress months, then ranks them by the farmer’s goals.

Benefits and impact. Fewer bare months and higher soil organic matter. Rotations that break pest cycles. Early, explained warnings before salt or drought hits. Advice that respects what each farm can actually do. The backup plan is always presented as a forecast that the farmer decides on, so it builds trust rather than replacing judgement.

Hardware. The optional TerraKey node is a solar-powered field sensor. It measures salinity (EC), soil moisture, water level, temperature and humidity, adding plot-level zones and live readings. All core features work on NASA data alone.

Tools.

  • App: plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS, Leaflet maps, Vercel hosting
  • Pipeline: Python with pandas, xarray, XGBoost and PyTorch (GPU)
  • NASA data access: Earthdata login, GES DISC OPeNDAP, AppEEARS and the ORNL DAAC MODIS web service

Creativity and design choices.

  • Built mobile-first and bilingual for farmers.
  • Uses plain words and icons instead of jargon.
  • Every number shows its source.
  • The app refuses to suggest crops into risky months.
  • The forecast is only shown because it beat the 25-year average on held-out years.
  • We designed for real constraints: slow-draining paddies, salty canal water, limited labour and missing buyers.
projectRefs: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 (salt tolerance)
